Amazon Web Services Training Module
Here's a detailed AWS training module designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of Amazon Web Services, covering core services, best practices, and hands-on labs to reinforce learning.

---

AWS Training Module Outline

Module 1: Introduction to Cloud Computing and AWS
   - 1.1 Basics of Cloud Computing
     - Cloud computing fundamentals (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS)
     - Benefits of cloud over traditional infrastructure
     - Cloud deployment models: Public, Private, and Hybrid
   - 1.2 Introduction to AWS
     - Overview of AWS services and global infrastructure
     - AWS account setup and basic billing structure
     - Understanding the AWS Management Console, CLI, and SDKs
   - 1.3 AWS Core Concepts
     - Regions, Availability Zones, and Edge locations
     - Shared Responsibility Model
     - AWS Free Tier and basic pricing models

Module 2: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
   - 2.1 Introduction to IAM
     - Understanding IAM users, groups, roles, and policies
     - Setting up users and implementing least privilege access
   - 2.2 IAM Policies and Permissions
     - Creating custom policies and understanding JSON structure
     - Policy evaluation logic and permissions boundaries
   - 2.3 Multi-Factor Authentication and Security Best Practices
     - Configuring MFA for users
     - Best practices for securing AWS accounts and IAM usage

Module 3: Compute Services with Amazon EC2
   - 3.1 Introduction to EC2
     - Understanding EC2 instances and instance types
     - Launching, configuring, and managing EC2 instances
   - 3.2 EC2 Storage Options
     - Configuring Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes
     - Snapshots and backups for EBS volumes
     - Introduction to Elastic File System (EFS) and S3 integration
   - 3.3 Scaling and Load Balancing
     - Configuring Elastic Load Balancer (ELB)
     - Setting up Auto Scaling groups for high availability
     - Monitoring instances with Amazon CloudWatch

Module 4: AWS Storage Services
   - 4.1 Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service)
     - Overview of S3 and use cases
     - Creating and managing S3 buckets
     - Storage classes and cost optimization
   - 4.2 Security and Access Management for S3
     - Setting up bucket policies and ACLs
     - Enabling encryption (SSE-S3, SSE-KMS)
     - Configuring S3 Lifecycle policies for data retention
   - 4.3 Advanced S3 Features
     - Versioning, cross-region replication, and transfer acceleration
     - Hosting static websites with S3
     - S3 Glacier and S3 Glacier Deep Archive for long-term storage

Module 5: Networking with AWS
   - 5.1 Amazon VPC (Virtual Private Cloud)
     - Creating VPCs, subnets, route tables, and internet gateways
     - Understanding CIDR notation and IP addressing in AWS
   - 5.2 Security Groups and Network ACLs
     - Configuring security groups for EC2 instances
     - Implementing network ACLs for additional control
   - 5.3 Advanced VPC Configurations
     - Setting up NAT gateways and VPN connections
     - VPC peering and inter-region VPC peering
     - Introduction to AWS Transit Gateway for large networks

Module 6: Databases on AWS
   - 6.1 Introduction to AWS Database Services
     - Overview of RDS, DynamoDB, and Aurora
     - Choosing the right database for your application
   - 6.2 Amazon RDS
     - Launching and managing RDS instances
     - Configuring backup, snapshots, and Multi-AZ deployments
     - RDS monitoring, scaling, and maintenance
   - 6.3 NoSQL with DynamoDB
     - Introduction to DynamoDB and data modeling
     - Implementing DynamoDB tables, indexes, and queries
     - Configuring DynamoDB Streams and triggers with Lambda
   - 6.4 Caching and Data Analytics
     - Using Amazon ElastiCache (Redis and Memcached)
     - Introduction to Amazon Redshift for data warehousing
     - QuickSight and data visualization

Module 7: Serverless Computing with AWS Lambda
   - 7.1 Introduction to Serverless Computing
     - Benefits of serverless architectures
     - Overview of AWS Lambda and common use cases
   - 7.2 AWS Lambda Functions
     - Writing, deploying, and managing Lambda functions
     - Using the Lambda console and AWS CLI
     - Configuring function triggers and permissions
   - 7.3 Serverless Integration
     - Using API Gateway with Lambda for REST APIs
     - Integrating Lambda with S3, DynamoDB, and SNS
     - Lambda best practices (cold starts, concurrency, and monitoring)

Module 8: Application Integration
   - 8.1 Amazon SQS (Simple Queue Service)
     - Setting up message queues and processing workflows
     - Configuring message retention, delay queues, and dead-letter queues
   - 8.2 Amazon SNS (Simple Notification Service)
     - Creating topics and managing subscriptions
     - Integrating SNS with Lambda, SQS, and mobile push notifications
   - 8.3 Amazon EventBridge
     - Using EventBridge to build event-driven applications
     - Setting up rules and targets for event handling
     - Integration with AWS services and custom applications

Module 9: Monitoring, Logging, and Optimization
   - 9.1 Amazon CloudWatch
     - Monitoring resources with CloudWatch metrics
     - Setting up alarms and automated actions
     - Using CloudWatch Logs for application logging
   - 9.2 AWS CloudTrail
     - Tracking user activity and API calls
     - Setting up CloudTrail and auditing activity logs
   - 9.3 Cost Management and Optimization
     - Using AWS Cost Explorer and AWS Budgets
     - Best practices for cost optimization
     - Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, and Spot Instances

Module 10: Security and Compliance
   - 10.1 Security Best Practices in AWS
     - Implementing AWS security best practices
     - Understanding security tools (AWS Inspector, GuardDuty, and Macie)
   - 10.2 AWS Key Management Service (KMS)
     - Creating and managing encryption keys
     - Integrating KMS with other AWS services
     - Overview of AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
   - 10.3 Compliance and Governance
     - AWS compliance programs (HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR)
     - Using AWS Config for compliance auditing and tracking
     - Implementing policies with AWS Organizations and Service Control Policies (SCPs)

Module 11: Deployment and DevOps on AWS
   - 11.1 Introduction to AWS DevOps Tools
     - Overview of CI/CD pipelines in AWS
     - Using CodeCommit, CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, and CodePipeline
   - 11.2 Infrastructure as Code with AWS CloudFormation
     - Creating and managing CloudFormation stacks
     - Writing and managing CloudFormation templates
     - Using AWS CDK (Cloud Development Kit) for code-based deployments
   - 11.3 Monitoring and Automating Deployments
     - Setting up auto-scaling policies and alarms
     - Monitoring deployments with CloudWatch and CodeDeploy
     - Implementing Blue/Green and Canary deployments

Module 12: Capstone Project and Certification Preparation
   - 12.1 Capstone Project
     - Designing and deploying a full-scale application (e.g., E-commerce or social networking app) on AWS
     - Utilizing multiple AWS services (EC2, S3, RDS, Lambda, etc.)
     - Implementing security, monitoring, and cost management
   - 12.2 AWS Certification Preparation
     - Overview of AWS certifications (e.g., Solutions Architect, Developer, SysOps)
     - Practice exams and study resources
     - Tips and strategies for passing AWS certification exams

---

Dot Net Core Training Module
Here’s a .NET Core training module that will guide learners from the basics of .NET Core to advanced development topics. The module covers essential topics, best practices, and hands-on projects to reinforce learning.

---

.NET Core Training Module Outline

Module 1: Introduction to .NET Core
   -1.1 Overview of .NET Core
     - Understanding .NET and .NET Core
     - Differences between .NET Framework, .NET Core, and .NET 5+
     - Advantages of .NET Core: Cross-platform, open-source, high performance
   -1.2 Setting Up the Environment
     - Installing .NET SDK and Visual Studio/Visual Studio Code
     - Setting up your first .NET Core project
     - Familiarity with Visual Studio tools and commands (CLI commands)
   -1.3 Basic .NET Core Application
     - Creating a "Hello, World!" console application
     - Understanding the structure of a .NET Core project
     - Overview of the Program and Startup classes

Module 2: C Fundamentals (for Beginners)
   -2.1 Introduction to C Syntax
     - Basic syntax and structure of C
     - Variables, data types, and operators
     - Control flow (if, switch, loops)
   -2.2 Working with Collections and LINQ
     - Lists, arrays, dictionaries, and sets
     - Introduction to LINQ (Language Integrated Query)
     - Common LINQ operations (Where, Select, OrderBy, etc.)
   -2.3 Object-Oriented Programming in C
     - Classes, objects, and inheritance
     - Encapsulation, polymorphism, and interfaces
     - Understanding namespaces and assemblies

Module 3: ASP.NET Core Basics
   -3.1 Introduction to ASP.NET Core
     - Differences between ASP.NET Core and traditional ASP.NET
     - Understanding MVC architecture (Model-View-Controller)
   -3.2 Building a Simple Web Application
     - Setting up an ASP.NET Core MVC project
     - Creating models, views, and controllers
     - Routing basics and URL structure in MVC
   -3.3 Dependency Injection in ASP.NET Core
     - Understanding dependency injection (DI) principles
     - Built-in DI in ASP.NET Core
     - Registering and resolving services

Module 4: Working with Data in ASP.NET Core
   -4.1 Introduction to Entity Framework Core (EF Core)
     - Overview of ORM (Object-Relational Mapping)
     - Setting up Entity Framework Core in an ASP.NET Core project
     - Creating and configuring DbContext and models
   -4.2 Database Migrations and CRUD Operations
     - Generating and applying migrations
     - Creating, reading, updating, and deleting records with EF Core
     - Using LINQ with EF Core for querying data
   -4.3 Working with Data Validation and Model Binding
     - Data annotations for model validation
     - Binding form data to models
     - Implementing custom validation attributes

Module 5: Web API Development in .NET Core
   -5.1 Introduction to RESTful APIs
     - Understanding REST principles and HTTP methods
     - Differences between MVC and Web API projects
   -5.2 Creating a Web API Project
     - Setting up a Web API project in ASP.NET Core
     - Building controllers and defining API routes
     - Working with JSON and XML serialization
   -5.3 Implementing CRUD in Web APIs
     - Implementing GET, POST, PUT, DELETE actions
     - Handling request/response status codes
     - Exception handling and returning appropriate error responses

Module 6: Security in ASP.NET Core
   -6.1 Authentication and Authorization Basics
     - Overview of authentication and authorization
     - Understanding Identity in ASP.NET Core
   -6.2 Implementing Authentication
     - Using ASP.NET Core Identity for user management
     - Registering, logging in, and managing users
     - Configuring roles and claims-based authorization
   -6.3 Securing Web APIs
     - Implementing JWT (JSON Web Token) authentication
     - Securing API endpoints with roles and policies
     - Handling cross-origin resource sharing (CORS)

Module 7: Advanced ASP.NET Core Features
   -7.1 Middleware and Custom Middleware
     - Understanding middleware pipeline in ASP.NET Core
     - Building custom middleware for logging, error handling, etc.
     - Ordering and configuring middleware
   -7.2 Logging and Exception Handling
     - Using built-in logging providers (console, file, etc.)
     - Configuring custom logging with third-party providers (e.g., Serilog)
     - Exception handling and creating custom error responses
   -7.3 Caching and Performance Optimization
     - Implementing in-memory caching and distributed caching
     - Response caching in Web APIs
     - Best practices for optimizing ASP.NET Core applications

Module 8: Testing and Debugging in .NET Core
   -8.1 Unit Testing in .NET Core
     - Setting up unit tests with xUnit
     - Writing tests for controllers and services
     - Mocking dependencies with Moq
   -8.2 Integration Testing
     - Setting up integration tests for APIs
     - Testing database interactions with EF Core
     - Testing authentication and authorization workflows
   -8.3 Debugging Tools and Techniques
     - Using Visual Studio debugging features (breakpoints, watch, etc.)
     - Debugging with logging
     - Troubleshooting common issues in .NET Core applications

Module 9: Deployment and Cloud Integration
   -9.1 Preparing for Deployment
     - Configuring app settings and environment variables
     - Setting up logging and diagnostics for production
     - Optimizing application for deployment (trimming, bundling, etc.)
   -9.2 Deploying to Azure
     - Creating an Azure account and setting up resources
     - Deploying ASP.NET Core apps to Azure App Service
     - Using Azure SQL Database with ASP.NET Core
   -9.3 Working with Containers
     - Introduction to Docker and containerization
     - Creating Docker images for .NET Core apps
     - Deploying Docker containers to cloud platforms

Module 10: Capstone Project
   -10.1 Project Overview
     - Planning and designing a full-featured web application (e.g., E-commerce platform, Blogging system)
     - Applying best practices learned in previous modules
   -10.2 Development Phases
     - Implementing MVC structure and Web API endpoints
     - Integrating authentication, authorization, and data management
     - Adding custom middleware and optimizing for performance
   -10.3 Deployment and Presentation
     - Deploying the project to a cloud platform
     - Demonstrating features and discussing project challenges
     - Reviewing code and final optimizations

Java Script Training Module

Here’s a comprehensive JavaScript training module that covers the essentials and advanced topics. This module is structured to help learners build a strong foundation in JavaScript, move on to more complex concepts, and apply them to real-world projects.

---

JavaScript Training Module Outline

Module 1: Introduction to JavaScript
   -1.1 What is JavaScript?
     - Overview of JavaScript's role in web development
     - History and evolution of JavaScript
     - Understanding the JavaScript ecosystem (browsers, Node.js)
   -1.2 Setting Up Your Environment
     - Installing a code editor (Visual Studio Code)
     - Setting up the console in browsers (Chrome DevTools)
     - Writing and executing your first JavaScript code
   -1.3 Basic Syntax and Structure
     - Variables and data types (let, const, var)
     - Basic operators and expressions
     - Comments and code organization

Module 2: Core JavaScript Concepts
   -2.1 Data Types and Variables
     - Primitives (String, Number, Boolean, Null, Undefined, Symbol)
     - Complex data types (Arrays and Objects)
     - Type coercion and type checking
   -2.2 Control Flow
     - Conditional statements (if, else if, else, switch)
     - Loops (for, while, do...while)
     - Breaking out of loops with `break` and `continue`
   -2.3 Functions and Scope
     - Declaring functions (function declaration, function expression, arrow functions)
     - Function parameters, arguments, and return values
     - Scope and closures
     - Higher-order functions and callbacks

Module 3: Working with Objects and Arrays
   -3.1 Understanding Objects
     - Creating and accessing objects
     - Adding, updating, and deleting properties
     - Object destructuring and shorthand properties
   -3.2 Array Manipulation
     - Array creation and manipulation (push, pop, shift, unshift)
     - Array methods (map, filter, reduce, forEach, find, some, every)
     - Working with multidimensional arrays
   -3.3 Object-Oriented Programming in JavaScript
     - Understanding prototypes and inheritance
     - Creating classes and objects using ES6 classes
     - Constructor functions and methods
     - `this` keyword and its behavior in different contexts

Module 4: DOM Manipulation and Events
   -4.1 The Document Object Model (DOM)
     - Understanding the DOM structure
     - Selecting elements (getElementById, querySelector, etc.)
     - Modifying element content and styles
   -4.2 Events in JavaScript
     - Event types (click, mouseover, input, etc.)
     - Adding and removing event listeners
     - Event propagation (bubbling and capturing)
     - Preventing default behaviors and using `stopPropagation`
   -4.3 Dynamic HTML with JavaScript
     - Creating, appending, and removing elements
     - Manipulating attributes and classes dynamically
     - Handling form submissions and validations

Module 5: Asynchronous JavaScript
   -5.1 Understanding Asynchronous JavaScript
     - Synchronous vs. asynchronous behavior
     - Callbacks and callback hell
   -5.2 Promises
     - Creating and using promises
     - `then`, `catch`, and `finally`
     - Error handling with promises
   -5.3 Async/Await
     - Converting promises to async/await
     - Handling asynchronous operations with async/await
     - Error handling in async functions
   -5.4 Working with APIs
     - Using the Fetch API to make HTTP requests
     - Parsing JSON data from APIs
     - Handling API errors and displaying data

Module 6: Advanced JavaScript Concepts
   -6.1 Error Handling and Debugging
     - Using `try`, `catch`, and `finally`
     - Throwing custom errors
     - Debugging with console statements and breakpoints
   -6.2 JavaScript Modules
     - Introduction to modules in JavaScript
     - Exporting and importing modules (ES6 modules)
     - Understanding default and named exports
     - Module patterns (CommonJS, AMD)
   -6.3 Working with Closures and the 'this' Keyword
     - Deep dive into closures and lexical scope
     - Binding `this` in functions (`call`, `apply`, `bind`)
     - Understanding arrow functions and their lexical `this`

Module 7: ES6 and Modern JavaScript Features
   -7.1 ECMAScript Overview
     - The evolution of JavaScript with ECMAScript standards
     - New features in ES6 and beyond
   -7.2 Key ES6 Features
     - Arrow functions, template literals, and destructuring
     - Default parameters, spread/rest operators
     - Enhanced object literals and concise methods
   -7.3 Advanced ES6 Concepts
     - Symbols and iterators
     - Generators and `for...of` loop
     - Proxy objects and Reflect API

Module 8: Testing and Debugging JavaScript
   -8.1 Introduction to JavaScript Testing
     - Importance of testing in JavaScript development
     - Types of tests (unit, integration, end-to-end)
   -8.2 Unit Testing with Jest
     - Setting up Jest for testing
     - Writing basic tests and test suites
     - Mocking functions and modules
   -8.3 Debugging JavaScript Applications
     - Using browser developer tools for debugging
     - Inspecting and monitoring errors in the console
     - Setting breakpoints and stepping through code

Module 9: Building a JavaScript Project
   -9.1 Project Planning
     - Choosing a project (To-Do App, Weather App, E-commerce site)
     - Breaking down the project into smaller components
   -9.2 Project Development
     - Setting up the project structure
     - Implementing key features (e.g., fetching data, updating UI)
     - Adding interactivity with event handling
   -9.3 Code Optimization and Final Touches
     - Reviewing and refactoring code
     - Adding responsiveness and accessibility
     - Final testing and debugging

---

React Native Training Module
Here's a sample React Native training module outline, designed to introduce learners to the fundamentals of React Native and guide them through building functional, engaging mobile applications.

---

 React Native Training Module Outline

Module 1: Introduction to React Native
   - 1.1 What is React Native?
     - Understanding cross-platform mobile development
     - Benefits of using React Native
     - Comparison with other frameworks (Flutter, Xamarin, NativeScript)
   - 1.2 Setting Up the Development Environment
     - Installing Node.js and npm
     - Setting up Android Studio, Xcode, and required simulators
     - Installing the React Native CLI
   - 1.3 React Native Basics
     - JSX in React Native
     - Components, Views, and basic layout structure
     - Running a simple "Hello, World!" app on iOS and Android

Module 2: Core Concepts and Building Blocks
   - 2.1 Components in React Native
     - Functional vs. Class components
     - Understanding Props and State
     - Lifecycle methods in Class components
   - 2.2 Styling
     - Flexbox in React Native
     - Inline styles vs. StyleSheet
     - Creating responsive layouts
     - Handling screen orientations and resolutions
   - 2.3 Navigation
     - Introduction to React Navigation
     - Setting up Stack, Tab, and Drawer navigation
     - Passing data between screens

Module 3: Working with APIs and Data Management
   - 3.1 Fetching Data from APIs
     - Introduction to REST APIs and JSON data
     - Fetching data using `fetch` and `axios`
     - Handling asynchronous code with `async/await`
   - 3.2 Managing State with Context API
     - Overview of Context API
     - Setting up a global state with Context
     - Using Context with functional components
   - 3.3 State Management with Redux
     - Basics of Redux (Store, Actions, Reducers)
     - Setting up Redux in React Native
     - Connecting components to Redux state
   - 3.4 Persistent Storage
     - Using AsyncStorage for simple data storage
     - Introduction to Realm and SQLite for more complex data

Module 4: Advanced Concepts and Enhancements
   - 4.1 Animations and Transitions
     - Introduction to basic animations in React Native
     - Using the Animated API
     - Implementing transitions between screens
   - 4.2 Forms and Input Handling
     - Creating forms and handling user inputs
     - Validating forms with Formik and Yup
     - Using TextInput, Picker, and custom inputs
   - 4.3 Handling Permissions
     - Accessing device features (camera, location)
     - Requesting permissions and handling permissions with `react-native-permissions`
   - 4.4 Working with Native Modules
     - Introduction to bridging and native modules
     - Using pre-built libraries with native code
     - Brief overview of building custom native modules

Module 5: Testing and Debugging
   - 5.1 Debugging React Native Apps
     - Using React Native Debugger and React Developer Tools
     - Debugging in the Chrome console
     - Common issues and troubleshooting techniques
   - 5.2 Testing in React Native
     - Unit testing with Jest
     - Writing snapshot tests
     - Introduction to end-to-end testing with Detox

Module 6: Deployment and Optimization
   - 6.1 Preparing the App for Production
     - Generating release builds for Android and iOS
     - Configuring app icons, splash screens, and launch screens
     - Handling app versioning
   - 6.2 Optimization Techniques
     - Improving app performance with lazy loading and memoization
     - Reducing app size by optimizing images and dependencies
     - Code-splitting and dynamic imports
   - 6.3 Publishing the App
     - Submitting an Android app to the Google Play Store
     - Submitting an iOS app to the App Store
     - Handling app updates and store requirements

Module 7: Capstone Project
   - 7.1 Project Overview
     - Building a full-featured app (e.g., To-Do List, E-commerce, Social Feed)
     - Using the skills learned in previous modules
   - 7.2 Project Development Phases
     - Planning the app structure and components
     - Implementing UI, data fetching, navigation, and state management
     - Adding final touches: animations, transitions, and forms
   - 7.3 Presentation and Review
     - Code walkthrough and best practices discussion
     - Optimizations and final checks
     - Demo and feedback session

1. Software Requirements

  • Operating System:

    • Windows 8.1 or higher (Windows 10 or Windows 11 is recommended).

    • Power BI Desktop is not available for macOS or Linux.

  • .NET Framework:

    • .NET Framework 4.7.2 or higher is required for Power BI Desktop to run.

  • Web Browser:

    • Any modern web browser (e.g., Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Safari) to interact with the Power BI service.

2. Hardware Requirements

  • Processor:

    • Minimum: 1 GHz or higher x86- or x64-bit processor.

    • Recommended: 2 GHz or higher multi-core processor.

  • RAM:

    • Minimum: 2 GB of RAM.

    • Recommended: 4 GB or more of RAM (especially for larger datasets and reports).

  • Disk Space:

    • At least 1 GB of available disk space for installation.

    • Additional space will be required for data storage (Power BI can handle large datasets, so more space is recommended if you're working with large data).

  • Display:

    • A 1024 x 768 screen resolution or higher is required.

    • For an optimal experience, a higher resolution (e.g., 1920 x 1080) is recommended.

3. User Account

  • Microsoft Account:

    • While you can use Power BI Desktop without a Microsoft account, having a Microsoft 365 or Azure Active Directory (AAD) account will allow you to access additional features such as Power BI Pro and Power BI Service.

  • Power BI Service:

    • To publish reports and dashboards to the cloud and collaborate with others, you will need a Power BI Pro license or an organizational Power BI Premium capacity.

4. Data Sources

  • Power BI Desktop supports a wide range of data sources, including:

    • Excel files, CSV, text, XML, JSON

    • Databases such as SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL, PostgreSQL, etc.

    • Cloud sources like Azure, Google Analytics, and Salesforce.

    • APIs and web services.

  • You may need to ensure that you have access to these data sources, as well as the appropriate connectors or drivers installed (e.g., for SQL Server or other databases).

5. Knowledge and Skills (Not strictly eligibility, but important)

  • Basic understanding of BI concepts such as data modeling, DAX (Data Analysis Expressions), and Power Query.

  • Familiarity with visualization best practices and how to design intuitive, actionable reports.

Course Title: Introduction to Data Analytics

Course Description:
This course provides a beginner-friendly overview of the principles and practices of data analytics. Students will learn how to collect, clean, analyze, and visualize data to make informed decisions. The curriculum introduces essential tools and techniques, including spreadsheets, SQL, and basic Python for data analysis.

Through interactive lessons, real-world case studies, and hands-on projects, learners will develop the skills to interpret data trends and communicate insights effectively. By the end of the course, participants will be able to apply data-driven thinking to a wide range of professional and academic contexts.

Key Topics Covered:

  • Basics of data collection and preparation

  • Introduction to databases and SQL

  • Data visualization principles

  • Using Python for simple analysis

  • Interpreting results and storytelling with data

Who Should Take This Course:
This course is designed for beginners with no prior experience in analytics. It is ideal for students, early-career professionals, and anyone interested in using data to solve problems and make better decisions.

Course Format:

  • Duration: 6 weeks

  • Mode: Online, self-paced with weekly assignments

  • Assessment: Quizzes, a mid-term project, and a final case study presentation
